# Basics

A paragraph right after a `#` divider becomes its subtitle, in every format.

## Text & inline formatting

Plain prose with **bold**, *italic*, and `inline code`. Hyperlinks look
like [Quarto docs](https://quarto.org). [Alerted text]{.alert} is
emphasized in the PDF and HTML decks; pptx renders it as plain text.

Bulleted list:

- First point
- Second point with `code`.  This point needs to be expounded upon very very verbosely to force a line wrap so we can see how spacing woks for wrapped bullets.
  - Especialy when there are multiple. And one also needs to be expounded upon very very verbosely to force a line wrap so we can see how spacing woks for wrapped sub-bullets.
  - Sub-bullets
- Third point

Numbered list:

1. Step one
2. Step two
3. Step three

## Math

Inline math reads like $E = mc^2$ inside a sentence.

Display math gets its own line. Amdahl's law:

$$
S(p) \;=\; \frac{1}{(1 - f) + f / p}
$$

where $f$ is the parallel fraction and $p$ is the processor count. PPTX
renders these natively as OMML equations. The PDF sets math in a serif math
font beside Poppins; `themeoptions: [fonts=bundled, mathfont=stix]` (or
`lm`, `pagella`, `sans`, `poppins`) picks another.

# Layouts

## Two-column layout

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="55%"}
**Left column — bullets:**

- Mix any block content
- Bullets, prose, tables
- Adjust width per side
:::
::: {.column width="45%"}
**Right column — code:**

```bash
mpirun -n 4 ./a.out
```
:::
::::

## Image embed

![A caption for the figure](images/example.jpg){width=60%}

Width can also be set in pixels (`{width=400}`) or with a `height=`
attribute. PNG, JPG, and SVG all work for HTML/PDF; PPTX prefers PNG/JPG.

## A linked screenshot

::: {.notes}
Wrap an image in a link and the picture opens the page in every format. Each
format also shows the URL: the HTML footer, a line at the foot of the PDF page,
and a caption box in pptx (link_captions.py). {height="72%"} is the full-width
screenshot recipe; it fits all three.
:::

[![](images/example.jpg){height="72%" fig-align="center"}](https://ncar.ucar.edu/)

## Full-bleed photo {.feature background-image="images/example.jpg"}

The `.feature` class makes the PDF and HTML decks a full-bleed photo slide
with the text on a translucent panel; pptx shows a plain title slide.

## Dark slide, step by step {.brand-dark}

`{.brand-dark}` sets an HTML slide on Space with white text; pptx and PDF
draw an ordinary slide.

::: {.incremental}
- `::: {.incremental}` reveals a list one item at a time
- in the HTML deck and the beamer PDF (one page per step)
- pptx shows the whole list at once
:::

## A short table, centered and scaled {.center scale="1.4"}

| Control | Moves |
|---|---|
| `.hcenter` | the body, across |
| `.vcenter` | the body, down |
| `.center` | both |
| `scale="S"` | its size |

::: {.notes}
`{.center scale="1.4"}` on the heading. Each control is independent; the
title, these notes and any † footnote are left alone.
:::

## A short list, filled {.hcenter .fill scale="1.3"}

- `.fill` grows the body until it just fits (HTML)
- `scale="1.3"` is what the PDF and pptx use
- `.hcenter` centers the list as a block

# Code & Diagrams

## Static code blocks

Bash, with syntax highlighting only (not executed):

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
module load intel openmpi
mpirun -n 8 ./solver --grid 256
```

Python:

```python
import numpy as np

def speedup(f, p):
    return 1.0 / ((1 - f) + f / p)

print(speedup(0.95, 64))
```

## Capturing live shell output

The fenced block below is **executed at render time** on the build host.
Both the command and its captured stdout land on the slide:

```{bash}
#| echo: true
hostname && which gcc && gcc --version
```

::: {.notes}
This runs when `quarto render` runs, not when the slide is shown. Output
is baked into the .pptx. Engine is `jupyter` with the `bash` kernel
(see frontmatter); `bash_kernel` is installed by `make conda-env`.
:::

## Mermaid diagram

::: {.notes}
Mermaid blocks render to PNG automatically for PPTX (configured in
`_quarto.yml`). Use `graph TD` for top-down, `sequenceDiagram` for
sequence diagrams, etc. The explanation lives in these notes, before the
diagram: text after an image would split the slide in pptx, and text before
it demotes the layout.
:::

```{mermaid}
graph LR
    SRC[Source code] --> CMP[Compiler]
    CMP --> EXE[Executable]
    EXE --> RUN[mpirun on Derecho]
```

## Graphviz diagram

::: {.notes}
Graphviz (`{dot}`) is built into Quarto, so there is nothing to install. Reach for it
over mermaid when grouping and ranking matter: its clusters keep their layout.
:::

```{dot}
//| fig-width: 9
digraph G {
  graph [rankdir=LR, fontname="Helvetica", fontcolor="#00357A"];
  node  [shape=box, style="rounded,filled", fontname="Helvetica",
         fillcolor="#E6F0FA", color="#0057C2", fontcolor="#00357A"];
  edge  [color="#6B7280"];
  subgraph cluster_hpc { label="NCAR HPC"; derecho [label="Derecho"]; casper [label="Casper"]; }
  subgraph cluster_svc { label="Services"; api [label="REST API"]; db [label="Database", shape=cylinder]; }
  derecho -> api; casper -> api; api -> db;
}
```

## Speaker notes

The body of this slide is short on purpose.

::: {.notes}
Speaker notes go inside a `::: {.notes}` div and appear in the PowerPoint
Notes pane (View → Notes), not on the slide itself. Use them for talking
points, citations, or reminders that shouldn't clutter the projected
slide.
:::

# Wrap-up

## Next steps

- Copy this file as a starting point for new decks.
- See `old.qmd` in this directory for a richer real-world example
  (database schema, REST API, deployment diagrams).
- Build with `make pptx` (also `make html`, `make pdf`) from this
  directory.
- Drop images under `images/` and reference them as
  `![](images/foo.png)`.

† A paragraph that starts with a dagger is a slide footnote: on the slide's
foot under a short rule in HTML and PDF, muted in place in pptx.

*‡ A second one stacks under the first, in order; emphasis is kept.*

## Thank you! {.closing}

The `.closing` class makes the PDF and HTML decks a closing slide on the
brand field, with this text under the headline; pptx renders it as an
ordinary slide.

# Backup

## Project config: `_quarto.yml`

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="55%"}
```{.yaml}
{{< include _quarto.yml >}}
```
:::
::: {.column width="45%"}
**What it does**

- Picked up automatically from the deck directory at render time.
- `format: pptx` + `reference-doc:` selects the NCAR-branded template.
- `slide-level: 2` makes `##` start a new slide; `#` is a section
  divider.
- `diagram.mermaid.theme:` themes auto-rendered mermaid diagrams.

**How it's shared**

- This file is a symlink to `../common/_quarto.yml`, so every deck
  inherits the same defaults.
- A deck that needs overrides can replace the symlink with its own
  real `_quarto.yml`.
:::
::::

::: {.notes}
The fenced block above uses Quarto's `{{< include _quarto.yml >}}`
shortcode — it pastes the file contents at render time, so the slide
stays in sync with whatever `_quarto.yml` actually looks like. Use the
same pattern for any small config or script you want to display
verbatim alongside commentary.
:::
